title: Complete proof of Erdos #202: Disjoint Covering Systems

problemStatement.formal: L_superlogarithmic: ∀ᶠ N, (log N)^c < L N where L(N) = exp(√(log N · log log N))
problemStatement.plain: Prove L(N) grows faster than any power of log N. For c ≤ 0 trivial; for c > 0, use exp(u) > u²/4 ≥ c²u for u ≥ 4c² where u = log(log N).
whyMatters: Fills analysis gap that Aristotle could not handle (type error)
Remaining 3 sorries are deep number theory results (E-S 1968, BFV 2013, Croot 2003)

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Proved L_superlogarithmic (4→3 sorries). For c ≤ 0: (log N)^c ≤ 1 ≤ L N. For c > 0: exp(u) > (1+u/2)² ≥ u²/4 ≥ c²u for u = log(log N) ≥ 4c², then c·u < √(exp(u)·u) = √(log N · log log N).
builtItems: Case c > 0: exp(u) > u²/4 via exp_add and add_one_le_exp
insights: Aristotle failed due to type mismatch (ℝ vs ℕ in L application) — not a mathematical difficulty
Key bound: exp(u) ≥ (1+u/2)² ≥ u²/4, so exp(u) > c²u for u ≥ 4c²
Remaining 3 sorries are deep number theory (Erdős-Szemerédi, de la Bretèche-Ford-Vandehey, Croot)
The file has good infrastructure: DisjointSystem, f, L definitions, density bounds all proved
nextSteps: The 3 remaining sorries require deep number-theoretic arguments beyond current Mathlib
